The gazelle dropped dung and urinated; then he released it. They slept during the noon rest and awoke, and there was a snake coiled around the belly of the man who had taken the gazelle. The snake did not leave him until there came from him of the account the like of what had come from the gazelle.

From Mujahid, who said: A group of traders from Syria entered Makkah in the Jahiliyyah and stopped at Dhu Tuwa. They baked a flat bread for themselves, but they had no condiment with them. A man among them shot a gazelle from the gazelles of the Sanctuary while it was grazing nearby. They went to it, skinned it, and cooked its meat to have with their bread. While their pot was boiling on the fire with the meat, a great tongue of fire came out from under the pot and burned all the people, but their garments, their goods, and the acacia trees under which they had been were not burned.

In the biography of Abu Rabi' ibn Salim al-Kula'i: a man from Kinanah ibn Hudhayl wronged his cousin, and he threatened him with supplication in the Sanctuary. He said: "This is my she-camel, so-and-so; ride her and go to him, and strive in supplication." He came to the Sanctuary in the sacred month and said: "O Allah, I supplicate You earnestly and in dire need against my cousin, so-and-so; strike him with a disease for which there is no cure." Then he departed and found his cousin had been struck in the belly, and he became like a waterskin, swelling until it burst.

And Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, asked a man from the Banu Sulaym about the loss of his sight. He said: "O Commander of the Believers! We were the Banu Dab'a, ten of us, and we had a cousin whom we wronged, and he would remind us of Allah and of kinship. When he saw that we would not refrain from him, he came to the Sanctuary in the sacred months and began raising his hands, saying:

"O Allah, I call upon You earnestly, / Kill the Banu Dab'a, not one remaining.
Then strike the man and leave him sitting, / Blind; when led, he exhausts the leader."

He said: My nine brothers died in nine months, one each month, and I remained, and I went blind, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, struck me in my leg, so no guide suits me." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: [Glory be to Allah, this is indeed a marvel!]

Allah made this in the Jahiliyyah, when there was no religion, to honour its sanctity and nobility, so that people would refrain from violating what He had forbidden, out of fear of swift punishment. When the religion came, the appointed time became the Hour, and Allah responds to whom He wills. So fear Allah and be with the truthful. End of quotation.

It seems that it was for such a reason that He expressed it with establishment (al-tamkin), and ﴿people are snatched from around them﴾, as its confirmation will come in the following verse. Before that it had been merely a patch of the earth's lands with no distinction over others in any kind of distinction. The meaning is: We did this only after Isma'il ﷺ (peace be upon him) had settled there, as a preparation for what We intended of wisdom and rulings. Is not He who was able to do that and did it for those who worship other than Him, able to protect those who enter His religion, who have become of His party through various kinds of protection, and to raise them above every one who opposes Him to the highest ranks? Just as He did in protecting you from them and from others, from all the opposing enemies of the religion.

When He described it with security, He followed it with what the soul seeks after it, saying: ﴿Are brought to it﴾, that is, gathered and drawn, from what they do not hope for and have no power to attract, ﴿to it﴾, that is, specifically, apart from others in the Arabian Peninsula, ﴿fruits of every thing﴾ from the plants that are in the land of the Arabs, from the fruits of hot lands such as dates in their early stage, ripe dates, bananas and jujube, and of cool lands such as grapes, apples, pomegranates and peaches. In His expressing it with the present tense and what follows it there is an indication of continuity, and that there comes to it after that from everything in the earth of wealth what had not occurred to anyone of them in thought. Allah has indeed spoken truly, as you see, and who is more truthful in speech than Allah?

Since the total of what He provided them in this Sanctuary of security, with its means of swiftly striking whoever commits harm in it with various kinds of punishment, and the gathering of these fruits, is in extreme strangeness in those dry, intensely hot lands, surrounded by people who follow no religion, fear no consequence, and have no dominant sovereign among the people to repel them, nor any order of human governance to prevent them, He, glorified is He, expressed it along with the manifestation of greatness with "from Us" (ladunna), saying: ﴿a provision from Us﴾, that is, from the most hidden and wondrous of what We have, in which no one has any making, as you know, you and those who follow you, and whoever among them has the capacity for guidance. All of that is only for your sake, by your alighting in this Sanctuary, latent in the loins and manifest in those valleys, as a preparation for your prophethood and a paving for your mission. Whenever you are absent from them, all that is absent from them too; and they will see.

Since what they put forward was an excuse for their failure to follow guidance, which they thought to be among the choicest of knowledge, the Exalted refuted it, negating from those among them who did not believe all of the knowledge, by whose negation this individual [claim] would cease to be knowledge. He said, in the style of emphasis for that: ﴿But most of them﴾, that is, the people of Makkah and others who have no guidance, ﴿do not know﴾, that is, they have no capacity for knowledge so that they would know that We are the ones doing that by arranging its causes until it was established and completed, so that no one has the power to change it; and We are able, if they follow Our command, to protect them from whoever wants them, rather We empower them over everyone who opposes them, as Our power to establish them is beyond the measure of what human intellects require. We are also able to strip all that away from them because of their persistence in disbelief. And We will surely make them taste all of it after your migration, so that they will know that it came to them only through your blessing. Had they known that, they would have been grateful; but they were ignorant and so disbelieved. For this reason they were warned: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [Sad: 88].

(p-327) When God, exalted is He, informed that He is able to grant security, deliverance, and establishment despite weakness, He followed this with an announcement of His power to inspire fear and to destroy despite strength. This was an encouragement for them, should they believe, toward the destruction of their opponents, and a warning, should they persist, against being treated contrary to their wishes. So He said, in the manner of majesty, joining it to the sense of the preceding speech: ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed﴾. It is also permissible for this to be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "We establish" (numakkin), meaning: We did to them what We mentioned of blessing despite their weakness and incapacity, while in fact We have destroyed the strong many times. He indicated the emphasis on abundance, together with specifying the vague term, by saying: ﴿from a town﴾. He indicated the cause of destruction by saying: ﴿that exulted in its livelihood﴾, meaning: exultation (baṭar) occurred from it during the time of its pleasant and ample life. Thus their state was like your state in security and abundant provision, but when they exulted over their livelihood, We destroyed them. The meaning of their exulting over it is that they split it open (shaqqūhā) by exceeding the limit in exuberance, insolence, and joy, until they went beyond it, so they corrupted it and were ungrateful for it, and did not give thanks for it. Rather, in receiving it they acted like one who is bewildered and stunned, so they did not properly care for it, and their capacity to bear the right of the blessance within it was small. They became insolent in turning about when it accompanied them, and they became arrogant with it, and they persisted in error in word and deed, because of the luxury that had overspread them, which turned them away from restraining it, and their capacity to bear wealth with it and the goodness of life within it was poor. So they nullified it through these traits, and they caused it to perish in vain without any return. This is from the statement of the lexicographers: al-baṭar (exultation): insolence and small capacity for bearing a blessing, and bewilderment, and transgression with a blessing; its verb, from all of these, is like faraḥa (to rejoice). The exultation of the truth is to be arrogant toward it so that one does not accept it. Baṭara him (with the verb pattern of naṣara and ḍaraba) means: he split it. Al-buṭūr means: the one who is loud and long-tongued, and the one who persists in error. Abṭarahu dharʿahu means: he burdened him beyond his capacity. Dhahaba damuhu baṭaran (with the vowel of kasr) means: his blood was lost in vain. Their exultation over it was that they disobeyed the One who had granted it to them, so they opposed His command, and pride made them forget the mention of Him for what He had given them.

(p-328) When this report led to the soul yearning to see the traces of these dwellings, He made consequent upon it an indication, using the demonstrative particle of distance, toward their dwellings, to draw attention to their abundance and to the ease of reaching them in every place, since they are in a place to which one can point, and to the distance of their rank in destruction, as evidence for the sentence that precedes it. So He said: ﴿Those are their dwellings﴾.

Since the meaning was that they lie in ruins with their roofs fallen, He connected to it His saying: ﴿not inhabited﴾, meaning: by any inhabitant, whether by choice or by compulsion. And since the intention was to convey the negation of both little and much time, He affirmed the preposition, so He said: ﴿after them﴾, after they had long exaggerated in them, embellished and adorned them, paraded brides in them, and rejoiced in great works.

﴿Except﴾ as a dwelling ﴿a little﴾, by passersby over them for an hour of night or of day. Then it becomes a ruin, desolate like deserts, after it had been a place of inaccessible protection, guarded by white swords and brown spears.

When these places became, after the ruin, one over which no one has any apparent disposal except God, and no ruler over them in what the eyes see except Him, and this was a great matter and a momentous affair, because in it there is no distinction between the exalted and the lowly, the small and the great, the sultan and the minister, He indicated its magnitude by saying, repeating the manner of majesty: ﴿And We are﴾ [i.e.] eternally and everlastingly ﴿We ourselves﴾, not other than Us, ﴿the Inheritors﴾. None has disobeyed Us, however great he is, nor has anyone delayed from Our purpose for a moment, however mighty it is. So would that I knew! Where are those tyrants, and how did their abodes become empty and their palaces become idle? By God, the arrogant ones, the cups of death destroyed them, with varied drinks of great calamities, and the sudden events of the days humbled them, by the power of the Mighty, the All-Knowing. Woe then to him who does not take warning from their days, and is not restrained from the like of their sins.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 59:**

When He, glory be to Him, displayed the whip of punishment in the hand of power, He indicated the treading of justice through the fruit of wealth. And because the verse is in the context of mercy through sending a messenger, He used the term Lordship (*ruboobiyyah*), saying: ﴿And your Lord was not﴾ [i.e., not in any way] ﴿one who destroys the cities﴾, i.e., the One who bestows favor upon you through sending you to mankind, ﴿destroying the cities﴾, i.e., this whole category, for a sin, however great it may be, ﴿until He sends into their mother﴾, i.e., its greatest and most noble, because the others follow it. It is not stipulated that he be from its mother, for ʿIsa, upon him be blessings and peace, was from Nazareth and was sent to Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿a messenger who recites to them﴾, i.e., to the people of all the cities, ﴿Our verses﴾, which indicate, through their conformity to the paths of reason, what is fitting for us of wisdom, and through their inimitability, which is singular in its word, and their dazzling greatness, as a binding of the proof and a cutting off of excuse, ﴿lest they say: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger"﴾ [al-Qasas: 47] (p. 330). For this reason, when We intended the generality of creation to receive the message, We made the Messenger from the Mother of All Cities, which is Mecca, the Sacred City. In it, because it is both a city where affairs proceed according to the law of wisdom and, in the lands of the desert, a place where the Word becomes manifest, I combined the two matters. The one sent to it is comprehensive, and it combined the two traces, because the seal is with him. The secret in making ʿIsa, who confirmed his religion, come from the desert, upon both of them be blessings and peace, is the great manifestation of the Word through his hands.

When He made the destruction conditional upon sending a messenger, as a warning, He set for it another limit, as a clarification and an explanation of the matter. And because the verse is in the context of the audacity of the people of misguidance, against the lofty station of the Messenger, through violating sacred things, He used the particle of majesty, saying: ﴿And We were not﴾, i.e., by Our majesty and self-sufficiency, ﴿destroyers of the cities﴾, i.e., all of them, ﴿after the sending of a messenger, except when its people are wrongdoers﴾, i.e., deeply immersed in wrongdoing through disobedience, by abandoning the fruits of faith.

When they made excuses for not standing firm in faith because of fear of being snatched away (al-takhattuf), He reminded them of His favour upon them by establishing the means of security and providing abundant sustenance. He made known to them that He alone is the One whose punishment should be feared, and whose seizing and striking should be guarded against by whoever opposes Him. Since their fear of the consequences of following the Messenger concerned either their own selves or the goods in their hands, it is certain from all of this that the implied meaning is: the consequences of wrongdoing, like the fate of the earlier peoples, are what caused the fear. So: your selves are in danger of destruction from the One who has power over you, just as He had power over those before you, because of refraining from following. This danger is greater than the danger of being snatched away because of following. Or the implied meaning is: what you feared of being snatched away does not harm you, and your holding back from following for its sake does not keep you eternal, so your destruction by God, in whatever manner it occurs, is not difficult for Him. He then joined to what the context guided us to supply, His saying: ﴿And whatever you have been given﴾, i.e., from [whatever] giver it may be, ﴿of a thing﴾, i.e., from these things that are in your hands and others, ﴿is the enjoyment﴾, i.e., it is the enjoyment ﴿of the worldly life﴾, and its benefit does not return to anything beyond it. It is subject to passing away, even if the period of enjoying it is long. ﴿And its adornment﴾, i.e., the adornment of the worldly life, all of which, let alone its adornment, is subject to perishing. Therefore it is neither eternal nor everlasting, nor is anything in it. ﴿But what is with God﴾, i.e., with the Supreme King, of what following produces for you of reward, which He has promised you in the Last Abode, the existence of which is clearly indicated by your unanimous description of this one as "the worldly." And who is more truthful in promise than God? ﴿Is better﴾, on the assumption that what is in the world shares with it in being good in your estimation, because what is with Him is more abundant, purer, more manifest, better, more desirable, more delightful, and more splendid. And it is, along with all of that, ﴿more lasting﴾ [An-Najm: 51], because although it shares with the enjoyment of the world in not being eternal, it is everlasting.

When it became clear that a sensible person would not expose himself to the mentioned danger of opposition out of fear of the described danger of following, the rebuke was directed at them in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 61:

When this became the cause for a great difference, as clear as the sun, to appear between the state of the one who opposes and the one who is in harmony, he made the following statement its consequence and result, confirming what was mentioned of the two matters (p-332), clarifying the distinction between them, and denouncing those who equate the two, let alone those who think that the state of the one who opposes is better: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise﴾ with Our greatness in wealth, power and truthfulness, ﴿a promise﴾ which is reward and recompense, ﴿good﴾, there being nothing better than it in its agreement with his wish and its lastingness, ﴿and he is going to meet it﴾ by means of Our promise, which is never broken, ﴿meaning he will certainly reach it and encounter it﴾, ﴿like one whom We have given enjoyment﴾, meaning by Our greatness, ﴿the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾, so that no one other than Us can take it from him without Our permission, and no one can make it last, and it, despite being transient, however long its span, is mixed with troubles and tainted with defilements and burdens. ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection﴾, which is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain, he who loses on it does not profit at all, and he who perishes cannot have a life in any way, ﴿he will be among those brought forth﴾, meaning those compelled to appear in a place, wishing that he could ransom himself from it with the earth filled with gold. For everyone who is assigned to attend a matter that causes distress is distressed according to the degrees of the assignment, whoever he is and whatever the matter is.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 62:

Since the day, though it is one, is multiplied by the multiplicity of its attributes, by what occurs within it and in its many parts, [the day of resurrection is referred to in this way] to magnify its matter and to exalt its gravity and evil, His saying, affirming the incapacity of the servants to offer any excuse on the Day of the servants, [is]: (p-333) ﴿And on the day He will call to them﴾, i.e., Allah will call to those who lured people and barred them from the path, who made excuses regarding the matter of faith and the oneness of the Beneficent Judge, ﴿and say﴾, i.e., Allah says: ﴿"Where are My partners?"﴾, i.e., from the idols and others. Then [He] explained that they do not deserve this name by His saying: ﴿"Whom you used to claim"﴾, i.e., in the sense that you were persistent in it, ﴿"to be"﴾, so that they might ward off from you, or from themselves.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 63:

Since the term "partner" (shari'k) applies to anyone other than God that a person takes as a partner in any matter, and since the followers had made the leaders whom they worshipped, from among the devils and others, equal to God in submission to them, in obedience in the worship of idols, in opposing the guides and hostility toward them, and in turning away from their followers, the term "partner" included them. The punishment for the one associated with God would fall first upon the one who counted himself a partner, and then upon the one who placed him in that rank. Thus the soul yearned to hasten to the answer by the leaders, out of fear that punishment would befall them and that they would be increased by their leadership over the others. So it was said: "They say," which is the original form, but He made it more apparent by informing of the attribute that made the saying necessary for them, and said: ﴿Those against whom the Word has come into effect (qala alladhina haqqa)﴾, that is, it was established and became obligatory, ﴿against them the Word [has come]﴾, that is, the meaning of this name and its application came upon them, namely the punishment promised with the greatest of words. They are the leaders of disbelief and the guides of ignorance, by their placing themselves in the rank of partners. The omission of the particle, as is the custom of those who are near (to God), and the expression by the attribute of goodness (p-334), indicates that after their vileness and arrogance they reached the extreme of humility and abasement. So He said, expressing their words: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray (ghawayna)﴾, pointing to the followers, that is, we caused misguidance (al-ighwa'), which is leading astray, to befall them, by the statements we adorned for them, which we helped them to accept as coming from us, although they were manifestly defective and clearly shameful, ﴿what You had granted us in this world of rank and wealth﴾. Then they resumed with what they supposed would repel (the punishment) from them, and said: ﴿We led them astray (aghwaynahum)﴾, that is, they went astray by their own choice, ﴿as we went astray (kama ghawayna)﴾, that is, we, when we were led astray by what was adorned for us from above us until we followed them, there was no compulsion or coercion from us, despite what the messengers had brought them and the intellects they possessed; just as we went astray by our own choice, there was no coercion upon us from those above us, as Iblis said: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]. The verse is of the type called ihtibak: the words "they went astray" were first omitted, due to the indication of ﴿ghawayna﴾ upon it, and secondly "since he led us astray, from before us" was omitted, due to the indication of ﴿aghwaynahum﴾ upon it and their intention. By this trivial statement they meant that there is in reality no blame upon us because of them, and this is the meaning of their words: ﴿We disown You (tabarra'na ilayka)﴾, that is, from their affair, so that no punishment is incumbent upon us because of them. This is a confirmation and explicit statement of what preceded.

Since they knew that they were not believers in their affair, they disowned being alone in misguiding them (p-335). So they said to one who seemed to ask: What is the nature of your disavowal, when you have acknowledged leading them astray?: ﴿They did not worship us (iyyana)﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿but they worshipped their own desires (kanu ya'budun al-awthan bima zayyanat lahum ahwa'uhum)﴾, although we did have some kind of calling them to it and urging them upon it. The least we desire is that the punishment be distributed upon everyone who was a cause of that, as in the other verse: ﴿So will you avail us anything against the punishment of God?﴾ [Ibrahim: 21]. The ignorant have forgotten that this does not benefit them at all against God, for all are in punishment, and none of them can avail another in anything. He said: ﴿For each there is double, but you do not know﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 64:

When he (Allah) did not turn to these words of theirs, but counted them as nothing, because there was no benefit in them, he indicated turning away from them, since they did not deserve an answer, as it is said: "Many a saying has its answer in silence." This is by His saying: ﴿And it will be said﴾, i.e., a second time, to the followers, in mockery of them and to show their incapacity, which entails their regret and the greatness of their grief. He expressed it in the passive form, to show contempt for them, and that they are so abased and humiliated that they respond to every command, whoever it may be from: ﴿Call upon﴾, i.e., all of you, ﴿your partners﴾, i.e., those whom you claimed, out of ignorance, to be partners (with Allah), so that they might ward off (the punishment) from you. He attributed them here to yourselves (lit. "to them," i.e., to you) to indicate that they did not gain from you the claim that they were partners of Allah, exalted is He far above that by a great exaltation, except that you made them partners in what you directed to them of your wealth, your words, your times, and your states. ﴿So they will call upon them﴾, making excuses with what does not avail, and clinging to what is certain not to profit, because of the overwhelming dominance and the seizure of bewilderment and astonishment. ﴿But they will not respond to them﴾, as is due to them by reason of their attribute of lacking perception, incapacity, and perdition. ﴿And they will see﴾, i.e., all of them, ﴿the punishment﴾, knowing that it will befall them with no barrier to keep it from them. So the situation at that time calls for anyone who sees them to say: ﴿If only they had been﴾, i.e., in a state that is a firmly established attribute of theirs, ﴿guided﴾, i.e., that guidance would come from them for an hour of time, out of regret for their condition and wishing for their deliverance; or, if that had been in their nature, they would have been saved from the punishment; or they would not have seen it at all; or they would not have followed them.

When he indicated that there is no escape from that ruin except through guidance, he followed it with the information that no one there can do what [might] deceive its questioner, as is done in this world, by displaying what has not been repeated, to magnify that day, make it dreadful, exalt it, and make it terrible. He asks about the right of His messengers, may blessings and peace be upon them, after asking about His own right, glorified is He, and he announces the powerlessness of the partners in the Hereafter, just as they were powerless in the first life.

﴿And on the day He calls out to them﴾, while they are within reach of the one calling and the sight reaches them, having all come forth before God, both those among them who were disobedient and those who were obedient, on one level plain, with the crowding having overtaken their breaths, feet piled upon feet, sweat having bridled them, and drowning having engulfed them, ﴿He will say, "What"﴾, that is, make clear or specify your answer which ﴿you gave to the messengers﴾, that is, with it.

(p-337)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 66:

Since they had no firm standing (qadam sidq) or prior claim to truth (sabiq haqq) regarding the proofs (hujaj) the messengers brought them, and the evidences (adillah) continued to pile up against them, they had no answer except silence. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Then the news became obscure to them﴾, that is: it was hidden and darkened by error (ghawayah) and obstinacy (lajaj). ﴿The news [i.e., the reports] upon them﴾: the reports that are of such magnitude that on that Day they deserve to be mentioned, and by which deliverance could be achieved. He used the preposition ʿalā (upon) to indicate that their blindness fell upon them, so that blindness encompassed all of them. Thus they came to be in a state in which the news could not find its way to them because of its being renewed (li-tajaddudiha), and they could not find their way to it because its blindness had spread over them. All of this indicates that they had not presented any deed worthy of being mentioned on that Day in response to the messengers; rather, they had put forward denial and harm, such that they would wish that between them and it (the Day) there were a vast distance. He said ﴿on that Day﴾ as a repetition to instill fear of that Day and to magnify its terror, and to affirm its greatness and exaltation.

When this questioning resulted in silence, knowing that none of them had anything that could suffice in answering with good speech and correct words, and that whatever statement they made would only return upon them with calamity, He said, translating this state: ﴿So they will not ask one another﴾, that is: none of them will ask another about anything by which deliverance might be obtained, because they know that destruction has encompassed them all, and ﴿there is no escape now﴾ (wa-la-ta hina manas), and because each of them is the most hateful of people to the other.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 67:

When the condition of those who persisted in their disbelief and did evil was made known through these verses, and the condition of those who repented, were promised the good promise, was indicated by a more subtle allusion, this led to a longing (tashawwuf) to state their condition explicitly. So he said, detailing and ordering according to what is implied: this is the condition of those who persisted in their disbelief. ﴿But as for him who repents﴾, that is, turns away from his disbelief, and says ﴿and believes﴾, explicitly stating what was understood by implication, for disbelief and belief are opposites, and one of them cannot be abandoned except by taking up the other. ﴿and does righteous deeds﴾, confirming his claim with his tongue, ﴿righteous﴾.

Since the soul is inclined to deficiencies and hastens toward lowly things, an allusion was made to the difficulty of persisting on the path of guidance except through great striving, by His saying: ﴿So perhaps﴾, that is, his attitude of hope arising from this condition is what leads to ﴿he will be﴾, that is, being in a state of utmost steadfastness, ﴿among the successful﴾, that is, those who are saved from the evil of that Day, those who attain all that is sought by continuing in their obedience until death. He did not state definitively that he would be successful, even though in the customs of kings such a thing would be definite, to inform that the Exalted is under no obligation to do anything, so that one's caution remains constant and one fears His decree and His destiny, for all is from Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 68:

When it was as if it were said: "What is the matter with the people of the first division that they do not seek deliverance from the straits of that calamity toward the spaciousness of this hope?" and the answer was: "Your Lord has prevented them from that," or "Has He not decided for the people of this division the attainment of success, as He decided for the people of the first division the attainment of misery?" and the answer was: "Indeed your Lord is not bound by anything." He followed it with a reference to Him, saying: ﴿And your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to you, by agreeing with whoever agrees with you and opposing whoever opposes you, for great wisdoms whose depths are beyond the understanding of most minds. ﴿Creates whatever He wills﴾ of guidance and misguidance and other things, because He is the absolute Owner, with none to prevent Him from anything of that. ﴿And chooses﴾, that is, He brings about choosing for whatever He wills, so He wills disbelief for the wicked and faith for the righteous, with none to object to Him. Perhaps one who showed repentance apostatized, because of what was written for him in the Book, and so became among the people of perdition. So do not grieve over whoever has escaped you, whoever he may be, and know that he harmed only himself, (p-340) and whoever escapes us, it suffices that we will overtake him.

When this made clear that whenever anyone other than Him, glorified is He, wills something, it is not but in agreement with His will, exalted is He, He stated it explicitly with His saying: ﴿They had no choice﴾, that is, that they should do, or that there be done for them, whatever they choose, such as the Messenger coming with the like of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought, or other than that. "Choice" (al-khiyarah) is a noun derived from "choosing" (al-ikhtiyar), used in place of the verbal noun, and it is also the noun of "the chosen." It is therefore an expression of the causer by the cause, because if it is left to itself it is barren, and so it is nothing. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': In this there is evidence that the servant, in his choosing, is not a chooser. Therefore the people of contentment set down their saddles before their Lord and submitted their affairs to Him with pure entrustment, meaning: if He commands them or forbids them, they hasten; if He strikes them with the great arrows of calamities, they endure; if He honors them, they honor themselves and are dignified; and if He humbles them, they are content and submit. So nothing pleases them except what pleases Him, and they do not will except what He wills and decrees:

"Passion halted me where you are, so there is for me neither one who lags behind it nor one who advances beyond it.

I find blame in your love sweet, out of love for your remembrance, so let the blamers blame me.

You humiliated me, so I humiliated myself in abasement; he whom you humble is not among those whom you honor."

Since inflicting something against His will is a deficiency, and the occurrence of association (shirk) is baseness and weakness, He, exalted, indicated the outcome of these verses in negating that from Himself, saying: ﴿Glory be to God﴾, that is, exalted is He who gathers the attributes of perfection, above anyone choosing something He does not will so that it reaches him or befalls him in some way. ﴿And exalted is He﴾, that is, He rose in the manner of one who strives in that, so His loftiness is such that minds cannot in any way attain the reality of His guidance. ﴿Above what they associate﴾, because there is no will for what they claim as partners; and even if they had a will, its execution would depend, in their weakness, on the creation of the Creator.

When power cannot be complete without knowledge, He said: ﴿And your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you and takes charge of your upbringing, just as He is perfect in power, so He is all-encompassing in knowledge. ﴿Knows what their breasts conceal﴾, that is, what they hide and keep secret: ﴿their breasts﴾ regarding whether they will believe if signs like the signs of Musa come to them, or will not believe, and regarding whether what some of them display of faith with their tongues is sincere or mixed.

Since knowledge of the hidden does not necessarily entail knowledge of the manifest, whether due to distance, noise, or a confusion of voices that prevents distinguishing one from another, or for some other reason, He said: ﴿and what they proclaim﴾, that is, what they make apparent. All of that is equal before Him, so nothing they intend can be outside His creation.

Since knowledge of that is only because He is God, and others know nothing of His knowledge except what He has taught them, He expressed this by His saying: ﴿He is Allah﴾, meaning the One who alone holds divinity, who has no namesake, and whose greatness no description encompasses beyond the general statement that He is great. As for the details, all of them or even a few, that is far, far beyond reach (haihat haihat). (p-٣٤٢) Then he explained the meaning of the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam) by His saying: ﴿There is no god but He﴾. Then he gave the reason for this by His saying: ﴿To Him belongs praise﴾, meaning to Him alone, ﴿in the first and the last [life]﴾, meaning the complete attribution of perfect qualities. This is not for anything besides Him, whether they believe or disbelieve. ﴿And to Him belongs judgment﴾, meaning the unrestricted execution of decree. Thus, had He willed to compel them to faith, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, meaning not to anyone else, ﴿with the least effort﴾, on the day of the blowing of the Trumpet, for the scattering of graves, through resurrection and rising up. Yet you are also now returning to Him in all your rulings and are confined to Him: if He wills, He executes them, and if He wills to reject and twist them, He does so. In these verses there is the utmost strengthening for the hearts of the obedient and the utmost deterrence and restraint for the rebellious, by alerting them that He is capable of all possibilities, knowing all knowables, exalted above deficiencies and afflictions, who recompenses the obedient and the disobedient with justice.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 71:

When [the verses] established the all-encompassing power and perfect knowledge, and that He alone is the God, whether they affirm His oneness or deny it, [and that these signs are] in this order, He presented a proof indicating all of that, by what was gathered in it of knowledge, wisdom and perfect power, alerting to the obligation of praising Him and detailing some of what He is praised for. So He said, placing the night first because its sign is negative (ʿadamiyya), and it is prior: ﴿Say﴾ to those who perhaps persist in denying this, rebuking them and binding them to the argument. He used the plural because it is more indicative of obligation and greater in silencing [the opponent], (p-343) so He said: ﴿Have you considered﴾, i.e., tell me, ﴿if Allah makes for you﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, looking to the station of greatness and majesty, ﴿the night﴾ by which the heat of the day is moderated, ﴿perpetual﴾, i.e., continuous. And He said: ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, to indicate that this is something against which denial cannot be directed, ﴿who is a god other than Allah﴾, the One of supreme station, for whom there is no equal?

Since light is a blessing in itself, and by it its Creator is known, He stated it explicitly and left its effect implicit, so He said: ﴿Will bring you light﴾, i.e., it will be born as day in which you disperse. And because of the strength of its informing about power and its making Allah known, He expressed it with this rather than "give you light." Since the night is the place of rest and the gathering of the senses, it is more conducive to hearing and more penetrating to thought. The Exalted said: ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾, i.e., to what is said to you, with attentiveness and reflection, as is the case for one who is in the night and benefits by his hearing, among people of intellect.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 72:

﴿Say: Have you considered: if God makes﴾ that is, He to whom all command belongs, in His majesty and dazzling perfection, ﴿for you the day﴾ whose heat balances the moisture of the night, so that through both the plants are made good, and all the other measured provisions are completed, ﴿continuously﴾ that is, perpetually, from ﴿sarad﴾ (continuity), which means succession, with the addition of the letter mim for emphasis, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ that is, a matter which no rational person would deny, ﴿who is a god other than God﴾ the Majestic, who has no equal, and who is ﴿over all things a Guardian﴾.

[p. 344] Since darkness is not sought for its own sake, and since after light it is most clearly indicative of His Unity, He turned away from His name and said, expressing the same kind of thing as before: ﴿brings you the night﴾ that is, which arises out of darkness. Then He made clear, by what indicates what He omitted from the first part, saying: ﴿in which you rest﴾. So the verse is of the type called ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two contrasting items are mentioned, each one omitted in one half and indicated by the other): He mentioned light first as an indication of the omission of darkness in the second part, and the night and rest in the second part as an indication of the omission of day and dispersal in the first part.

Since light is something through which the eye can penetrate, He said: ﴿Will you not see?﴾ that is, with sight and insight, how the veils of darkness are lifted from the bright, noble faces of light, and then wrap themselves in the black mantles of modesty; and the faces of the lights and the brightness [Ibn Hubayra said: al-Mubarrad said: the authority of hearing is in the night, and the authority of sight is in the day].

When the intended sense was: "So from His wisdom He made for you hearing and sight, so that you might contemplate His signs and observe His creations," He joined to it ﴿And from His mercy﴾, i.e., the mercy that encompasses everything, not from any other source, such as fear, hope, or attachment to some purpose among purposes. ﴿He made for you the night and the day﴾ as two great signs, through which and by which He arranged all your interests, and He stored up the greater part of His mercy for the Hereafter. (p-345) He erased the sign of the night ﴿so that you may rest in it﴾, i.e., so that you do not strive in your livelihood. And He made the sign of the day "sight-giving," "so that you may seek of His bounty," by striving in your livelihood with your effort. So the verse contains ihtibak (interlacing, a figure in which one element is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, and then the omitted element of the first is mentioned and the mentioned element of the second is omitted). He first mentioned rest as an indication of the omission of striving in livelihood in the second part, and second mentioned seeking as an indication of the omission of not striving in livelihood in the first part.

When he had mentioned this blessing which He bestowed through this mercy, and had mentioned the reason for His making it in the stated manner, he mentioned another reason, which is the one intended in itself, because it is the result of hearing and sight, the two faculties whose use he had earlier urged. So he said: ﴿so that you may be thankful﴾, i.e., so that your state would be the state of one from whom gratitude is hoped for, because of the continual succession of the blessings mentioned, which come to you from the Benefactor through your receiving them by these two faculties, and because of what He arranged for you out of kindness toward you in what He ensured for you, in the abode of causes, concerning the affairs of livelihood and the return: the rest through stillness after what He conferred upon you of profits and gifts through dispersal and movement. As for the Hereafter, since it is not built upon causes, and since the Garden contains no toil in any respect, there is no need in it for the night.

When He mentioned what the successful one has of hope on the Day of Recompense, and followed it by informing that guidance to success comes only through Him, and indicated through that the mention of the days of this world, which comprise night and day, in a manner indicating His oneness, informing of the power over resurrection after death by the repeated origination of each of the two alternating (al-malawayn, night and day) after its non-existence, and the repeated causing of people to die through sleep, then raising them through wakefulness, and concluded that with thankfulness, indicating that it is the cause of success, He returned to the Day of Recompense, in which the fruit of all that appears, reproaching polytheism despite the manifestness of these proofs of tawhid and the absence of any doubt supporting polytheism other than mere imitation. So He said, alerting to their incapacity to produce proof when proof is due, on the Day of Calling, in the presence of the witnesses, along with what it contains of emphasis for terror through repetition, and confirmation for the affirmation of the declaration of God's oneness and its establishment: ﴿And on the day He calls to them﴾, i.e., these who think they can escape, ﴿then He says﴾ with the tongue of anger, disgrace and rebuke, and they have been gathered in a gathering: ﴿"Where are My partners"﴾. He repeated the indication that their associating is only in name, with no meaning in it at all, so He said: ﴿"whom you used to"﴾, i.e., with utmost effort, until that became a firm habit for you, ﴿"assert"﴾, with no doubt for you in that when verified at all.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 75:

When he (Allah) had mentioned the first proof, among the proofs for the refutation of association (shirk), that the partners did not answer them, nor did they have any power to help them or to help themselves, and it might have been said that this was due to something other than incapacity, He here pointed to the matter of association without any shadow of doubt in the evidence. He said, [turning the speech to the manifestation of the first person in the style of majesty, because it is pure action]: ﴿And We will draw out﴾, that is, We will single out with power and might, ﴿from every nation a witness﴾ (p-347), that is, their own messenger, who will bear witness against them concerning their deeds and what they were in of confusion in the snares of association.

When their questioning about their evidence for their association followed from that, He said: ﴿Then We will say﴾, that is, to the nations: ﴿Produce your proof﴾, that is, your decisive evidence to which you resorted in the world and upon which you relied in your polytheism, as is the way of people of intellect, who do not build anything on a foundation that is not sound. ﴿Then they will know﴾ by means of [this] questioning, when they are compelled, so they search and strive, but find for themselves no support at all, ﴿that the truth﴾, that is, concerning divinity, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King to whom all command belongs and who has no equal, with no partner for anything beside Him. ﴿And what they used to invent will have vanished from them﴾, that is, it will have gone away and been nullified, the absence of a lost thing, ﴿from them﴾, that is, a condition which was like a nature for them, ﴿that they used to fabricate﴾, that is, they used to say it as the saying of one who lies deliberately, since it has no evidence and no doubt that would cause error concerning it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 76:

When He had shown their incapacity in that abode, and their knowledge that the one who disposes of all decrees is only the One, the Subduer, He showed that this is also true of Him in this abode: the occurrence of knowledge of Him through the destruction of the people of insolence, exultation and vestiges, without those they misled being able to avail anything, and without anyone who misled them, whether speaking or silent, being able to avail them. This is an application of the generality of ﴿How many a town We destroyed that had exulted in its livelihood﴾ [al-Qasas: 58] to some particular cases, as a warning to whoever denied the Prophet (ﷺ), especially whoever attributed him to sorcery, and as an announcement that the prophets, upon them be prayers and peace, cut off the wretched even if they were the closest of relatives. For He, glorified is He, punished Qarun and those with him with a punishment that no one before them had received, and they were from the Children of Israel and among the closest of the Children of Israel to Moses, upon him be prayers and peace. Thus it becomes known to everyone who was deceived by what he had been given that the truth belongs to God in everything that His messengers called to and His books spoke of, and that what they relied upon failed them and did not avail them anything. Their object of worship in reality was what they had gathered of the debris of this world, and they believed that through it they had attained lasting happiness and enduring honour. Such a thing, as will come in the next verse, is like the likeness of the spider which takes a house. All of this happened before the eyes of Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, when Qarun denied him, attributed him to sorcery, and behaved arrogantly toward him. So Moses did not ask God Most High concerning him, because by his arrogance he had left the promise of favour toward those who were oppressed [in the land]. The punishment with which they were punished was of the same kind as that with which Pharaoh was punished in form, in that it is an engulfing, although that was in a liquid and this is in solid ground, so that it might be known that He is capable of what He wills, so that fear of Him may endure, concerning what has preceded from Him of decree and destiny. Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, took from each tribe of the tribes of the Children of Israel a witness from among their own, and said to them: "Bring your proof [concerning it]." Then, by the flashing of Aaron's staff, upon him be prayers and peace, and not their staves, they knew that the truth belongs to God in the matter of priesthood (al-hubūrah) and in all His affairs. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun﴾, who is called Qurah in the Torah. Then He explained the reason for the emphasis with His saying: ﴿was﴾, that is, a firmly established state ﴿of the people of Moses﴾, as an alert that he deserved to be denied this state, because he did toward them what almost no one does toward his own people. That is because he was among those who believed in him, and concerning them We had said ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed﴾ [al-Qasas: 5], to the end of the verse, since he was a cousin of Moses, upon him be prayers and peace, as related by Abu Hayyan and others from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. ﴿So he oppressed them﴾, that is, he transgressed the limit in belittling them, with what We had bestowed upon him of this crumbling debris and perishing accident. So he cut off the bond between himself and them, and joined himself to Pharaoh and his like in the separation. That removed him from the sphere of favour, trust and inheritance into the circle of destruction, baseness and treachery, just as Pharaoh oppressed them. The original meaning of this ﴿baghā﴾ was "he intended," but since the servant should not have a will of his own, and the will belongs to his Master, as He pointed out in ﴿The choice was not theirs﴾ [al-Qasas: 68], his intention was made to be transgressing the limit, and it was construed with ﴿ʿalā﴾, which implies elevation, as an alert that it has departed from its original meaning.

When He mentioned his oppression, He mentioned its real cause, and said: ﴿And We gave him﴾, that is, and together with Our having favoured him by making him one of Our chosen, We gave him, by Our greatness, ﴿of the treasures﴾, that is, the hidden, stored wealth, in addition to the apparent wealth which is ready to be spent from for whatever matters might arise, ﴿such that﴾, that is, that which, or a great amount that cannot be enclosed, to the point that ﴿its keys﴾, that is, the keys of the locks behind whose doors it is buried, ﴿would indeed weigh down﴾, that is, would bend with effort and hardship because of their heaviness, ﴿a band﴾, that is, a large group whose members strengthen one another (ya'sibu). In the exaggeration expressed through the words "treasures," "keys," "weigh down," and the described "band," there is what shows that he was given of that more than anyone else among those of his rank was given, and all of this is something the intellects find hard to accept, so the emphasis came. ﴿Possessors of strength﴾, that is, they would bend them because of the weight they placed upon them. Al-Razi said: "Al-nawʾ is inclination. Al-nawʾ is also a star that inclines away from view at its setting. It is said: 'he rose with the load' when he got up carrying it heavy, and 'the load weighed him down' when it inclined him because of its weight."

When He mentioned his oppression, He mentioned its time. A time may be broad, as we say: "such and such happened in such and such a year." In this there is an allusion to the cause, so He said: ﴿When his people said to him﴾. He said ﴿his people﴾ as an indication of the extremity of his oppression through his boasting and arrogance toward his relatives, whose custom is that their speech does not anger, does not kindle resentment toward them, and does not carry anything but counsel and compassion. Attributing the speech to all of them was permissible, although the speaker was some of them, as the following indicates, either by counting the silent one as a speaker because he consented to it, since it is something no one would reject, or because the people of goodness are the people, and whoever is other than them is nothing. ﴿Do not exult﴾, that is, do not be glad with a gladness that digs into your heart and penetrates it, so that it turns you toward insolence and exultation. For exulting in a passing accident indicates reliance upon it, and that indicates forgetfulness of the Hereafter, and that indicates the utmost ignorance, levity, and little reflection upon consequences, so it leads to exultation, and exultation leads to destruction. Al-Razi said: "Whoever rejoices in what is not something to be rejoiced in acquires a grief that has no end." They gave the reason for their prohibition with what conveys the utmost compassion and love, saying, emphasizing it in order to express the unlikelihood that one who sees the continuous flow of pleasing blessings upon someone would not be loved: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, so nothing is more majestic than Him, and it is toward Him that one should rejoice. ﴿Does not love﴾, that is, is not treated as one treats the beloved, ﴿the exultant ones﴾, that is, (p. 352) those firmly established in exultation over what perishes, for their exultation indicates the lowness of their aspirations.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 77:

Since abandoning exultation (al-farah) is a cause of asceticism (zuhd), and asceticism is the means of drawing near to God, it is as if it were said: "Be ascetic regarding it, for God loves the ascetics." ﴿Seek﴾, that is: seek with a seeking that exerts your soul in it, ﴿with what God has given you﴾, that is: the Great King to whom all command belongs, from these wealths while you have the means, ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾, by spending it on what God loves, in such a way that your seeking of that is enclosed within it, so that it is like the spirit, and the thing sought is like the body, that it may be alive through that seeking, so that nothing from it occurs without life. For your action toward that reminds you that this abode is a dwelling of departure and transience, and everything in it is headed to extinction, and that requires asceticism toward all the wealth in it.

Since that is very difficult for souls, together with what it contains of a taint of suspicion, they said: ﴿And do not forget﴾, that is: do not leave it in the manner of one who forgets, ﴿your share of the world﴾, leaving it in the manner of one who is neglected. Rather, make use of the permissible things: foods, clothing, marriage, dwellings, and what suits them. Let your use of these be, as the context indicates, without extravagance and without arrogance that would cause you to abandon the quality of equity (al-inṣāf). And from ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him: "Do not forget your health, your strength, your vigor, and your wealth, that with it you seek the Hereafter."

Since moderation in enjoying provision was permitted to him, and the soul is disposed to greed, so that if it is granted a speck of the world it makes it the greatest of the great, they followed this with what may restrain its greed, and said: ﴿And do good﴾, that is: bring about goodness by giving wealth to the needy and spending in all acts of obedience, ﴿as God has done good﴾, that is: the One who combines the attributes of perfection, clothed in the mantle of greatness and majesty, ﴿to you﴾, by giving as one who does not fear poverty, just as He has bestowed abundance upon you.

Since it is in the nature of the soul, if it is not restrained by the reins of the Law, to be extravagant and oppressive, they said: ﴿And do not seek﴾, that is: do not desire any kind of ﴿corruption in the earth﴾, through stinginess or wastefulness, or through arrogance toward the servants of God or contempt for them. Then He followed this with its cause, emphasizing it, because most corrupters are given expansion in the world, and most people find it unlikely that expansion would be given in it to one who is not beloved. So it was said: ﴿Indeed God﴾, that is: the All-Knowing of everything, the All-Powerful over everything, ﴿does not love the corrupters﴾, that is: He does not deal with them as one deals with one whom He loves, so He does not honor them.

When it was among the things they said that the one who gave him that (wealth) was none other than God, and his blessing had made him so arrogant toward his Creator that there arose a longing for an answer to his claim, it was said in an emphatic style, because every person knows from himself his own weakness, and that others would deny him what he claims he obtained by his own strength: ﴿He said, "I was only given it on account of knowledge"﴾, that is, this wealth, "that is with me." So I deserve it, and that knowledge is the cause of its acquisition, and no one has any favor over me in it. This is what the phrase "only" (innamā) conveys. The verb's construction in the passive voice indicates that he did not know who the Giver was. It has been said that this knowledge is alchemy (al-kīmiyā').

Since the implied meaning is: should he not fear that God would strip him, as a punishment for this, of his knowledge, his wealth, and his self? Does he not know that this is only by God's power? He has no real role in it at all, because God has impoverished one greater than him in cunning and more knowledgeable, and has given more than him to one who has neither knowledge nor power. He is able to destroy him, to take away what he has, and to annihilate him, just as He was able to give it to him. Then He joined to this His saying, rebuking him: ﴿Did he not know that God﴾, that is, with the attributes of majesty, greatness, and perfection that He has, ﴿had destroyed﴾ ﴿from before him﴾. By including "min" in His saying ﴿from before him﴾, He draws attention to the fact that he did not take warning, even though he witnessed those who were destroyed, who were described in this way, despite the nearness of the time. Had He omitted it, the destruction with that attribute would have encompassed all the time that preceded him, ﴿of the generations﴾, that is, those who were like hard rocks in their steadfastness, ﴿who were mightier than him﴾, that is, generations ﴿in strength﴾, that is, in body, and in meanings such as knowledge and others, and in helpers and servants, ﴿and greater in gathering﴾ in wealth and men. The last of them was Pharaoh, who consulted him about his kingdom, and confirmed his matter on the day of his destruction [important]. He used to enslave people like him and subject them to the worst torment. He did not treat them as one treats those he loves, nor was he prevented from doing so by any knowledge or any gathering among them. Rather, He seized them for their transgression and condemned their turning and their striving.

When it was the custom of the people of this world that, when they are angry at someone and wish to destroy him, they rebuke him, sometimes he swears to deny the sin and it is accepted from him even if he is lying, and sometimes the matter is uncovered that his inner affair is contrary to what appeared of his evil, so that he has a hidden excuse. Glorified is He, He indicated that this is not done except by one ignorant of the realities of affairs and the measures of the punishment deserved for every sin. He who is informed of the inner thoughts and the hidden secrets is free from that. So the Exalted said, mentioning the state of the object, which is ﴿from﴾ ﴿and not﴾, that is, He destroyed them while they were not asked, this being the basic rule. But He said ﴿is asked﴾, that is, by any questioner, ﴿about their sins, the criminals﴾. He made the cause for destruction explicit, to convey that what necessitates destruction is criminality, which is severing what ought to be joined, and joining what ought to be severed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 79:

Therefore, after their good admonition and their harsh reply, He (glory be to Him) linked and followed with His words, as evidence of his (Qarun's) transgression and his insolence in his sins: ﴿So he went out before his people﴾, that is, those who advised him regarding moderation in his affairs and abundance in generosity toward his brethren. Then He mentioned his condition, magnifying it by His words: ﴿in his adornment﴾, that is, the adornment that befits what we have mentioned of his wealth and his self-magnification in his perfection through his deeds and words.

Since it was as if it were said, "What did his people say?", it was said: ﴿Those who desired the life of this world said﴾, that is, they are such that there constantly arises in them the desire ﴿for the life of this world﴾, owing to the baseness of their aspirations and the limitation of their outlook to the perishing, because they were people of ignorance. Although their statement was in the category of ghibta (wishing to emulate a blessing without wishing it removed from its possessor), not of hasad (envy), which is wishing the removal of the blessing from the one envied: ﴿Would that we had﴾, that is, we wish with a great wish that we were given, from whatever giver and in whatever manner it might be, ﴿the like of what Qarun was given﴾ of this adornment and what results from it of knowledge, so that we would never cease to be possessors of wealth. Then they magnified it by their words, emphasizing (their claim) because they knew that whoever desires the Hereafter would object to them: ﴿Indeed, he is one of great fortune﴾, that is, of portion and fortune in this world, ﴿great﴾, by what he was given of the knowledge which was the means for him to all this wealth.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 80:

It indicates their ignorance, the excellence of divine knowledge (al-ʿilm al-rabbani), and the worthlessness of what Qarun was given of wealth and of apparent knowledge (al-ʿilm al-ẓahir), which led him to follow it. [It is indicated] by His saying: ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said﴾. He magnified the desire for knowledge by using the passive form (al-bina' lil-maf'ul), as an indication that it is beneficial in every respect [and in respect of asceticism (al-zuhd), and by describing the people of asceticism with it]. So He said: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾... [no, see below]. "Those who had been given knowledge" means: from among his people. Their souls were exalted above desiring the world, knowing its passing, as a deterrent for whoever wished for a similar state to his, and as an aspiration toward the Hereafter for its permanence. ﴿Woe to you!﴾ means: how strange for you! Or: evil has befallen you with certainty. The origin of "woy" (wayl) is "wayy" (ويْ). Al-Farra' said: the particle of the genitive (lam al-jarr), with a fatha, is placed after it with a pronoun, as in "wayy laka" and "wayy lahu," meaning: how strange for you and for him! Then the lam was merged with "way" because of frequent usage, until it became part of the word itself, so that it became inflected (mu'rab) by completing it as a triliteral. Therefore another lam could enter after it, as in "waylan laka," since the first became the lam of the word. Then it was transferred to the category of the mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence), so it was said "waylun laka," and it remains as it was in the state of nasb (accusative), since the original of "waylun laka" is: "halakta wayln" (you have perished, woe), meaning: destruction; so they raised it after deleting the verb, shaking off the dust of occurrence. It was also said: the origin of "wayl" is the supplication for destruction, then it was used for rebuke, deterrence, and urging to abandon what is not approved, just as "la aba laka" (may you have no father)—whose origin is a supplication against a man—is used to urge an action. So it is as if they said: "What is with us, that woe befalls us?" Then they informed them of what is fitting, turning away from [the desire] for which they deserved woe, as a belittling of what had enticed them until they said it. So they said: ﴿The reward of Allah﴾, meaning the Majestic, the Great, ﴿is better﴾, meaning than this chaff (al-hutam). Whoever loses the good, woe befalls him. Then they explained its recipient, to magnify it and encourage the listener toward its state, so they said: ﴿for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning confirming their faith ﴿righteous﴾. Then He, glory be to Him, explained the greatness of this counsel and the loftiness of its rank by His saying, emphasizing (that) the people of the world deny that they are not patient: ﴿But none receives it except the patient﴾, meaning: He does not make one who meets these words, or the counsel that the people of knowledge uttered, i.e., one who acts upon it, ﴿except the patient﴾, meaning: those who are patient over the decree of their Lord in ease and hardship, and who restrain themselves to acts of obedience, those for whom patience has become a character trait. He expressed it in the plural to encourage cooperation, indicating that religion, because of its difficulty, is not sustained by one individual alone.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 81:

When his looking (at his wealth) had as its consequence this, which led him to disbelief in his Lord, He seized him with punishment, and He (glory be to Him) indicated this by His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾, meaning: by the greatness that belongs to Us, ﴿him and his home﴾, meaning: and his home is in accordance with the measure of what We have mentioned of his greatness in his wealth and adornment. It is therefore a great matter, containing a numerous host and great furnishings, lest someone say that the sinking of him was out of desire to seize his wealth. ﴿The earth﴾, and he was of the people of Moses, peace be upon him, and very close to him, as the historians have related. So beware, O community of this Prophet, lest you reject the mercy that has come to you through his message, and so perish, even though you are the closest of people to him. For the prophets, just as they cannot place guidance in the hearts of the enemies, likewise they cannot prevent them from ruin, nor will they intercede for them at all, once they have realized that they are among the people of wretchedness. ﴿So there was not﴾, meaning: as a result of that, there was not ﴿for him﴾, meaning: for Qarun. The negation is emphasized, since it is firmly established in minds that the great are helped, by the addition of the preposition in His saying ﴿any group﴾, meaning: a company of people who would come back to him after what had overwhelmed him had alarmed them. The root of fi'ah (group) is a flock of birds, as if it was so named for the frequency of its returning and its speed in going back to the place from which it departed. ﴿to help him﴾.

Since Allah the Exalted is higher than everything, He said: ﴿besides Allah﴾, meaning: the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, clothed in greatness and majesty, because whoever was of his opinion perished, while whoever was among the friends of Allah watched over Allah in his affair, so they did not ask Allah about it, and he himself knew that the truth belongs to Allah, and what he used to invent went astray from him, as in the verse before it. ﴿And he was not﴾, meaning: he was not ﴿among those who defend themselves﴾ by their own strength.

[p. 360] When the earth swallowed him up, those ignorant people, who were like beasts that see nothing but sensible things, came to their senses. He expressed their condition with His words: ﴿And it became morning﴾, meaning [p. 360] "and it came to be." He used this expression to contrast it with "yesterday," and to inform that what they had seen of his condition filled their hearts, so that they had nothing else in mind. ﴿Those who had wished﴾, meaning they desired with great longing to be ﴿in his place﴾, meaning that his state and rank in this world would be theirs. ﴿Yesterday﴾, meaning the recent past, even if it was not the day immediately preceding their present day. ﴿They said, "Wayka'anna..."﴾. This word and the one after it are joined according to the consensus of the mushafs (codices). It is reported from al-Kisa'i that one stops on the ya' of wa, and from Abu 'Amr that one stops on the kaf: wayka. Al-Radi said in his commentary on al-Hajibiyya: wai expresses regret or wonder. Then he said: according to al-Khalil and Sibawayh, "wai" is an expression of wonder, combined with "ka'anna," which is used for comparison. Al-Farra' said: it is an expression of wonder to which the second person kaf is attached, as in "wayka 'Antar aqdim," meaning from his verse in the famous mimiyya poem, one of the seven Mu'allaqat:

Indeed, the saying of the knights, "Wayka, 'Antar, advance!", has healed my soul and cured its sickness.

That is: woe to you, and marvel at you. "An" was added to it, so the meaning is: "Did you not see that...?" Ibn al-Jawzi transmitted this from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. Al-Farra' said: Since the meaning of wayka'anna became "did you not see," the kaf of address was not changed for feminine, dual or plural, but remained in one form. Al-Ju'bari said in his commentary on al-Shatibiyya: "wai" is a sound uttered by one who regrets or marvels, and "wayka" originally is "waylaka," whose lam was dropped for lightness because of its frequent use; the kaf is for address, and "an" is vowelled with fatha because of the implied knowledge. Qutrub said: [it is fatha] because of the presumed lam. From the combination arose the meaning: "We regret our negligence, we marvel at our condition, and we realised the opposite of what we believed." It was written joined to signal the combination. Al-Qazzaz said in his comprehensive collection: wayka is a word by which a person draws attention; it is also said its meaning is mercy, and wai means alerting and disapproval. Imam 'Abd al-Haqq said: wai is a word said in wonder and in correction; it is also said wai means grief. Qutrub said: wai is an expression of lamentation. End of quotation.

Sibawayh said, in the section on what the predicate takes the accusative after the five particles: I asked al-Khalil about this verse, and he claimed that it is wai separated from ka'anna, and the meaning is: it happened that the people became aware and spoke according to their level of knowledge, or they were alerted, and it was said to them: "Does it not seem that this is so with you?" (And Allah knows best.) As for the exegetes, they said: "Did you not see that Allah...?" So the meaning that unites these sayings is: wonder, or woe, or regret for what we said, in clarifying our error and alerting to the mistake; or destruction for us; or disapproval directed at us; or grief for us; or lamentation over us; or correction of us; or mercy for us; or awakening from us; or admonition to us. Then they gave the reason for this by saying: "That Allah...," or "It seems that Allah...," or "Did you not see, O hearer and beholder, that Allah...?" Al-Razi said: it is a name given to speech, meaning "How wonderful!", and its meaning is alerting. Then he began with ka'anna: ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the Supreme King to whom all command belongs, ﴿extends provision﴾, meaning abundantly, ﴿to whom He wills﴾, whether or not he has means by which to seek provision.

Since the story is about Qarun, and he had the power in this world mentioned earlier, and it was customary that someone like him becomes arrogant and may lead him to self-deification, He said, alerting by means of his being struck down in the manner mentioned, that he was one of His servants, with no distinction between him and the weakest of them in relation to His power: ﴿of His servants﴾.

Since He showed that the extension is only from Him, He followed it with another proof of His lordship: ﴿and restricts﴾, meaning He straitens for whom He wills, whether he is shrewd or not. He does not extend it to anyone out of honour for him, nor does He restrict it on anyone out of contempt for him. Extension and restriction indicate neither humiliation nor honour. This is evidence that they thought Qarun's claim was correct, that he was given it on knowledge possessed by him, and that they only wished for his knowledge, which, in their belief, necessarily brings wealth in every condition.

Since it became clear to them from this event that provision is only in the hand of Allah, they followed it with what shows that they also believed Allah is able to do what He wills, beyond provision, just as He is able to provide. From their saying: ﴿Had not Allah been gracious﴾, meaning the Supreme King who alone possesses the attributes of perfection showed favour, ﴿to us﴾ by His generosity, so that He did not give us what we wished of being in a state like his, ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us﴾ as He caused it to swallow him. ﴿Wayka'annahu﴾, meaning: "How wonderful!" or "Regret!", because, or "It seems that," or "Did you not see that"... Al-Radi said in his commentary on al-Hajibiyya: the addressee was claiming that they would prosper, so he said to them: "How wonderful you are!" He was asked: "Why do you marvel at him?" He said: "Because..." etc., so he omitted the preposition with "an," as is the standard analogy.

﴿Will not prosper﴾, meaning will not attain his aim, ﴿the disbelievers﴾, meaning those who are deeply rooted in disbelief in the blessing of Allah. With this, the meaning is understood to be as they said concerning the intended sense of wayka'annahu, whether one stops at wai, or wayka, or does not stop.

Mention of the explanation of this story:

Al-Baghawi said: the scholars of reports said: Qarun was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel after Musa, peace be upon him, and the best reciter of the Torah, the most handsome and the richest of them; so he transgressed and rebelled. The first of his transgression and disobedience was that Allah the Exalted revealed to Musa, peace be upon him, that they should attach to their cloaks four threads, with a green thread at each end, the colour of the sky, to remind them of Me when they look at the sky, and to know that I send down My speech from it. [p. 364] Musa said: "O Lord! Will You not command them to make all their cloaks green, for the Children of Israel despise these threads?" His Lord said to him: "O Musa! Indeed the small of My command is not small; if they do not obey Me in a small matter, they will not obey Me in a great matter." So Musa summoned them, that is, informed them, and they complied, but Qarun was arrogant. This was the beginning of his disobedience, transgression and rebellion. When Musa crossed the sea with the Children of Israel, he gave the hubburah (priesthood) to Harun, peace be upon him, which is the leadership of the altar. The Children of Israel would bring their offerings to Harun, and he would place them on the altar, and fire would come down from the sky and consume them. Qarun said: "O Musa! To you belongs the prophethood and to Harun the priesthood; you are of no account, while I read the Torah. I have no patience with this!" Musa, peace be upon him, said to him: "I am not the one who assigned it to Harun, but Allah assigned it to him." Qarun said: "By Allah, I will not believe you until I see its proof." So Musa gathered the staffs of the leaders, bundled them, and placed them in his tent, where he worshipped Allah, and they stood guard over it. In the morning, Harun's staff had green leaves sprouting, and it was of almond wood. Qarun said: "By Allah, this is no more wondrous than what you do of magic." He mentioned matters in which he took pride, and that he threw a great thing at Musa, peace be upon him. Then Allah became jealous for Musa, peace be upon him, and caused the earth to swallow him.

[p. 365] What I have seen myself in the Torah, in the Fourth Book, reads as follows: "The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: Make tassels on the corners of your garments throughout your generations, and let the tassels that you make on the corners of your garments be of blue; and these tassels shall remind you of the commandments of the LORD so that you may do them and not follow your own heart, nor your eyes, and that you may be holy to the LORD your God. I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt; I am the LORD your God."

After these matters, Korah, which is Qarun's name in Hebrew, son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, of the sons of Reuben, rose up before Moses, with two hundred and fifty men from the children of Israel, leaders of the congregation, renowned and famous by name, mighty men. These, all of them, gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them: "You take too much upon yourselves, for all the congregation is holy and the LORD is among them; why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?" —that is, Aaron would be the priest, the one in charge of [p. 366] the offering and the judge over the service of the tent of meeting— When Moses heard this, he fell on his face, and he spoke to Korah and all his company, saying: "In the morning the LORD will show who is His and who is holy, and will cause him to come near to Him; the one whom He chooses He will cause to come near to Him. Then he commanded them to bring censers. He said: O sons of Levi! Is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel to bring you near to Himself, to do the work of the tabernacle of the LORD, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them? Since He has brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Levi with you, do you seek the priesthood too? Therefore you and all your company are gathered together against the LORD; what is Aaron that you grumble against him?" Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and they said: "We will not come up. Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you should also make yourself a prince over us? Moreover you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come up." Then Moses was very angry and said to the LORD: "Do not respect their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, nor have I wronged any of them." Then he said to Korah: "You and all your company be present before the LORD, you and they, and Aaron, tomorrow. Let each of you take his censer and put incense in it, and each bring before the LORD his censer, two hundred and fifty censers; you also, and Aaron, each with his censer." So they each took his censer, put fire in them, laid incense on them, and stood at the door of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
