Korah gathered all the congregation against them at the door of the tent of meeting. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the congregation. The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: "Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment." But they fell on their faces and said: "O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, will one man sin and You be angry with all the congregation?" So the LORD spoke to Moses, saying: "Speak to the congregation, saying: Get away from the tents of Korah, Dathan and Abiram." And Moses said: "By this you shall know that the LORD has sent me to do all these works, for I have not done them of my own will. If these men die the common death of all men, or if they are visited by the fate of all men, then the LORD has not sent me. But if the LORD creates something new, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them up with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into Sheol, then you will understand that these men have despised the LORD."

Then, when Moses had finished saying this, the earth split open beneath them. It opened its mouth and swallowed them, their tents, and all their livestock, and they went down alive into the pit. Then the earth closed back over them. All of the Children of Israel fled when they heard their cries and saw what had been done to them, saying, "Perhaps the earth will swallow us too." Fire came out from before the Lord and burned the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense. (p-368) After that day, the congregation of the Children of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying to them, "You have killed the people of the Lord." They turned toward the Tent of Meeting, and saw that the cloud had covered the Tent and the glory of the Lord had appeared. Moses and Aaron came and stood in the Tent of Meeting. The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them, "Get away from this congregation, for I will destroy them in a moment." They fell on their faces. Moses said to Aaron, "Take a censer in your hand, put fire and incense in it, and go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, for the wrath of the Lord has gone out against the whole congregation, and the plague has begun among the people." Aaron did as Moses commanded, went out to the congregation, saw that the plague had begun among the people, offered incense to the Lord, made atonement for the people, and stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stayed. Those who died in the plague numbered fourteen thousand and seven hundred men, besides those who had perished in the earthquake. Aaron returned to Moses at the Tent of Meeting, and the Lord spoke to Moses and said to him, "Speak to the Children of Israel and take from them a staff from each tribe, a staff for each, and write the name of each man on his staff, and write Aaron's name on the staff of the tribe of Levi. Place them in the Tent of Meeting before the Ark of the Testimony, where I meet with you. The man whom I choose, his staff will blossom, and I will relieve you of the grumbling of the Children of Israel against you." Then Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony, and saw that Aaron's staff had sprouted, put forth shoots, blossomed, and produced almonds. Moses brought out all the staffs, and they looked at them. The Lord said to Moses, "Return Aaron's rod to before the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious sons, so that their grumbling against Me may cease and they do not die, and so that no one other than the two sons (i.e., the tribe of Levi) performs the service of the Tent of Meeting. As for the Children of Israel, that is, the rest of them, they shall not draw near to the Tent of Meeting, lest they be punished and die." Then he mentioned the death of Aaron, peace be upon him, on Mount Hor, and the succession of his son Eleazar in his place in the office of the priesthood. End of quotation.

This is similar to what Allah did for our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) concerning the trunk of the palm tree that moaned, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) choice that Allah restore it to its best state as it was while alive, or place it in Paradise; he chose that it be in Paradise. Likewise is the case of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, when he overtook the Prophet (ﷺ) on the road of the Hijrah to bring him back, and his horse's legs sank into the ground until it went down to its belly three times. However, since the Prophet (ﷺ) was a Prophet of mercy, he did not curse him, and that sufficed to ward off his evil. He embraced Islam afterward, in the year of the Conquest, and the Prophet (ﷺ) gave him the good news that he would wear the bracelets of Kisra, and so it happened. Worse than the sinking that swallows the one who is swallowed, more painful, more shameful, and more disgraceful, is the story of the man who apostatized, was struck down, and was buried, but the earth rejected him. Al-Bayhaqi narrated at the end of the Dala'il (Proofs of Prophethood) from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There was a man from the Banu al-Najjar among us who had memorized al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, and he used to write for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he fled and joined the People of the Book, and they raised him up and admired him. Not long after, Allah broke his neck. They dug a grave for him and buried him, but the next morning the earth had thrown him up onto its surface. [Then they dug again and buried him, but the next morning the earth had thrown him up onto its surface.] So they left him exposed." He said: Narrated by Muslim in the Sahih. And from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, something similar concerning a Christian man whom the earth rejected three times before they left him.

He said: Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Sahih.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 83:

When Allah, glorified is He, had mentioned that the successful one (al-muflih) is he who repents, believes and does righteous deeds, and the scholars have indicated that this is the one for whom there is the reward of Allah, and that this was a cause (sabab) and a consequence (musabbab) for the Hereafter; and he had passed over what must be passed over, until He mentioned the story of Qarun, which makes known, as it must, that this abode is for passing away, in which neither men nor wealth avail, and that the Hereafter is for permanence; and He had commanded in it that seeking (al-ibtigha') in the affairs of this world be done well; and He concluded that this success is denied to the disbelievers. So this was the place for summoning the Hereafter to mind, although He had just previously mentioned it, and its agreement with what He had filled the ears with, so He made it present to every person of understanding and magnified in the sight of every person of knowledge. He indicated it, glorified is He, for both matters: presence and greatness, and He said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the matter that is seen by every eye, present in every heart, great in station, far-reaching in fame, high in rank, whose news has been heard and whose descriptions and traces have settled upon the ears, ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾, i.e., whose proofs are more than can be counted and clearer than can be explained and mentioned; among the greatest of them is that every person expresses his life by the world. And it is the one which Qarun was commanded to seek, but he refused except through haughtiness and corruption. ﴿We shall give it﴾ by Our majesty ﴿to those who﴾ act contrary to his deeds.

Since the greatest aim is the purity of the heart, from which the action of the limbs arises, He said: ﴿do not desire﴾, and He did not say "do not engage in" for example, (p-372) magnifying the harm of corruption by warning against everything that causes it, informing that souls inclined toward it and eager for it, so whenever they graze near it they will inevitably plunge into it. ﴿Haughtiness﴾, i.e., any degree of haughtiness, ﴿in the earth﴾, for it is the greatest pathway to corruption. And if they desire some of that in what appears to you when they command the good or forbid the evil, their intention is the elevation of the word of Allah through leadership in the religion, not their own elevation. ﴿Nor corruption﴾ by doing what Allah dislikes; rather they are in opposition to what Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun were upon, of humility together with leadership, for the sake of carrying the religion on their behalf, so that they may have the like of the reward of whoever is guided by them, not for any worldly portion. The sign of elevation for the sake of leadership, and not corruption, is that they do not take the servants of Allah as servants, nor the wealth of Allah as a private possession (duwal). The governing principle is acting in what pleases Allah, honoring the command of Allah, and abstaining from the world.

Since this has explained the state of those who fear the majesty of Allah, the Exalted, He, glorified is He, informed that He always makes their victory the final outcome, and He said, expressing it in the nominal form to indicate permanence: ﴿And the final outcome﴾, i.e., the last state that follows all states for them in this world and the Hereafter; this is the basic form, but He made it general and informed of the attribute that produced this for them, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿for the God-fearing﴾, i.e., always in both abodes, not against them. From the lam one knows that it is praiseworthy. And this verse distinguishes (p-373) the people of the Hereafter from the people of this world: whoever is ascetic regarding the first life, striving in righteousness, and tested in the beginning of his circumstances yet victorious in his wealth, then he is of the children of the Hereafter; otherwise he belongs to this world.

Now, when the distinction between the people of the two abodes has become clear, and it was necessary that the Hereafter come, and it is known that the Hereafter is only the recompense of deeds, and it has been established from its being for those who fear that it is for those who are secure, the detailing of that was resumed as an answer to one who seems to have said: "What is for those who do good and those who do evil upon arrival?" by His saying: ﴿Whoever comes with the good deed﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter or in this world, ﴿with the good deed﴾, i.e., the righteous state, ﴿for him there is﴾ from the bounty of Allah ﴿better than it﴾, by ten times, up to seventy, up to seven hundred, up to what none but Allah the Exalted encompasses. ﴿And whoever comes with the evil deed﴾, which is what Allah has forbidden, including frightening the believers, ﴿then those who did the evil deeds will not be recompensed﴾ except by one who is recompensed in some measure. The pronoun that returns to "whoever" was made apparent in this act, so He said: ﴿those who did the evil deeds﴾, depicting their state to make it ugly and to repel from doing it. Perhaps He gathered here and used the singular at first to indicate that the evil-doer is the majority: ﴿except the like of it﴾, equal, as an act of justice from Him, Exalted is He. This was the original form, but He said: ﴿what they used to do﴾, i.e., with all their resolve, ﴿they used to do﴾, as an intensification of the equivalence. This is (p-374) in the Hereafter. The verse also adds an indication that He does likewise in this world, even if it is hidden. They will be frightened in their sanctuary by what they used to frighten the believers with, and He has made it a place of security. They made excuses for not entering His religion out of fear of being snatched from their land, so their not entering it will become a cause of their fear and of being snatched from their land, and they will know that the security they were in was only because of you. Then on the Day of the Conquest they will be in your grip.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 85:

When he had established the mention of the Hereafter, which is the final return, and repeated it, affirmed the recompense therein, and that the ultimate outcome belongs to the God-fearing, he followed it with what serves as a kind of rationale for that. He said, beginning a new sentence (isti'naf), confirming and emphasizing what had been fixed in their minds of denying the Hereafter, and what the state of his departure ﷺ from holy Mecca necessitates regarding the improbability of his return to it: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained﴾, i.e., made obligatory, ﴿upon you the Qur'an﴾, i.e., the one that gathers what is scattered of excellences and details what is obscure of all meanings. That is, He ordained upon you all that is in this Book, which comprises both unification and differentiation, in a way that makes its good reception evident, through recitation, conveying, challenge, and action. He bound you and others with these obligations, and imposed upon you those duties, among them engaging in combat with swords, ﴿will surely return you﴾ (p-375) i.e., after death, because of the difficulty of what He has imposed upon you and bound you to of its hardship, ﴿to a place of return﴾, i.e., a great return. How great a return it is! He will recompense every person in it according to what he did. Your Lord will raise you therein, as a reward for your excellence in action, to a praiseworthy station, for which the first and the last will envy you, in return for what you endured in this matter of hardships that mountains cannot bear. Were it not for the return to this place of return, these obligations, most of which people do not act upon in most of their parts and for whose violation no one is requited, would be a futility, and it is known that a sensible human is far removed from that. How then could the Most Wise of the wise be so? So strive in what you are engaged in, for the glory of that Day, for the ultimate outcome is yours. This verse is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281], ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28], [﴿To God is your return﴾ [Hud: 4]], and other verses besides.

It is also permissible to say: "to a place of return," meaning: what place of return? A place which, by its greatness, is worthy that everyone who left it intends to return to it, namely holy Mecca, your worldly homeland. Thus Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, interpreted it, as al-Bukhari transmitted from him. It is a return which, by its majesty, is worthy to be mentioned, for your entry into it with armies by which Islam will be strengthened, and by which disbelief and its people will be humbled permanently. And the adorned Garden is (p-376) your otherworldly homeland, in the most perfect and highest, most honored and most excellent manner.

So do not suppose that He will lead you on the path of your two fathers, peace be upon them both: Abraham in his emigration from Harran, the city of disbelief, to the holy land, after which he did not return to it; and Ishmael, in being carried from the holy land to something holier than it, after which he did not return to it. Rather, He will lead you on the path of your brother Moses, peace be upon him, to whom He sent down the Book, just as He sent down to you the Book, the Qur'an, the Criterion, and with whom they associated you in their saying: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?﴾ [al-Qasas: 48]. (He led you) in returning him to the land which this surah mentions, as a preface to this verse, that he had left it in fear, watching and waiting, namely Egypt, for Midian at the borders of the lands of the Arabs, in a manner by which He destroyed his enemies: as for those who were not of his people, by drowning in the water; and as for those who were of his people, by the earth swallowing them. He honored his allies from among his people and others. Likewise, you left your city, Mecca, in fear, watching and waiting for the noble city of Medina. However, your return, because you are the Prophet of mercy, and because your departure was not caused by killing any of them, will not entail their destruction, but rather their might, security, wealth and stability. The wording of the Qur'an was chosen over the Book, because of what it contains of the gathering that entails dispersal (al-nashr), as already passed in al-Hijr. Thus the context, which concerns dispersal, gathering, and separation from his city and then reunion, is fitting. It is related that this verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ at al-Juhfah, which lies on the route of the emigration (hijrah).

Since it was understood from the emphasis of this assertion that there are those who exaggerate in negation and denial in proportion to this emphasis in affirmation, saying: "The matter is not so, and he will not return to Mecca while there is an eye that blinks among us," He said, threatening, by way of a new sentence (isti'naf), on his tongue ﷺ, because the denial is a rejection of him, just as Moses ﷺ was rejected when he answered with the like of that, as has preceded: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., to these deniers of what I have told you: ﴿My Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is benevolent to me, ﴿knows best﴾, i.e., more than anyone.

Since this story is accepted without dispute by any sensible person who affirms the Creator, and they used to say: "Whoever claims his return is astray," the question turned toward the one who is guided to the right course and the one who is astray. This is witnessed by the conquest of Mecca upon their approach, along with those lions, the heroic champions and the noble chieftains. So He said, in the form of a question, to show fairness and to distance from accusation: ﴿Who has brought guidance﴾, i.e., the one than whom none is clearer: is it I, in what I have brought from my Lord, in this speech whose inimitability God bears witness to for me, that it is from Him? Or are you, in what you say, from yourselves? ﴿And who is in manifest error﴾, i.e., are you in your speech, which is plainly flawed, of great shame and great disgrace, or am I? ﴿Manifest﴾, i.e., clear (p-378) in itself, making evident to everyone whatever flaw is in it, even if the one who follows it strives to conceal it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 86:

When the answer applies to everyone who is fair-minded: "They are in clear error, because they fabricate from their own selves what has no evidence for it, whereas you have brought guidance, because you brought it from Allah," he built upon this his saying: ﴿And you were not⦆ (ﷺ)... [the sentence continues below].

It is also permissible for the clause to be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun in "ʿalayka" (upon you), with what lies between them being an interjected parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ) for the sake of emphasis in refuting the one who denies the Return (maʿād). That is: He imposed it upon you while you were not [expecting it].

It is also permissible to say: since his return to Makkah was extremely remote, owing to the great number of the disbelievers and the scarcity of helpers, He brought it near to him with His saying, informing that many matters occur without expectation, and even contrary to analogy: ﴿And you were not hoping﴾, i.e., in the bygone age and in any state of the states, ﴿that the Book would be cast﴾, i.e., would descend in a manner that could not be prevented, ﴿to you﴾. That is: with this belief, nor with any part of it; this was not part of your affairs, nor did anyone ever hear it from you on any day of the days, nor did you prepare for it its customary preparation, such as learning writing or sitting with a scholar, so that some kind of accusation could approach you, as His saying Exalted is He in the verse that follows indicates: ﴿And you did not recite before it any Book﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 48], and so on. The word "Book" was chosen here because the context concerns mercy, of whose fruits is the firmly established gathering (p-379), and that is the signification of the Book. Then He said: ﴿except﴾, i.e., but rather the Book was cast to you ﴿as a mercy﴾, i.e., for the sake of a great mercy to you and to all creatures through you, which you had not been hoping for ﴿from your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who bestows favour upon you by making you chosen for that, through calling to it and concentrating aspirations upon it. He expressed it with the particle of the connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) to indicate that his state before prophethood, of purity from worshipping idols, from drawing near to them, from swearing by them, and from all indecencies, and of devotion to Allah through seclusion with Him and worship of Him, was by Allah's grace a state of one who hopes for that.

Since what has preceded caused diligence in [stirring the aspirations to devote themselves to] the command of Allah, out of hope for what He, Glorified is He, has of reward, and in gratitude for the sending down of the Book, He said in a context of emphasis, because human nature inclines to perceive the support of the disbelievers against a matter of such great grace, owing to their multitude, strength and might: ﴿So never be [then] by reason of their multiplicity⦆ a supporter (ẓahīr), i.e., a helper ﴿to the disbelievers﴾ by dwelling among them, or by slackening in striving in calling them, out of despair of them because of what you see of their remoteness from response, even though your warning has lasted long. Do not grow weary, as We have not grown weary. For We have conveyed the word to them and followed up exhortation and narrative for them, and We are able to destroy them in a moment and to guide them in the briefest glance; and just as Mūsā, upon him be prayers and peace, after being favoured, was not a supporter of the criminals. This is a training from Allah Exalted for the leaders of the community in calling to Allah when opposition is great and the allied helper is few.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 28, verse 87:

Since slackness in forbidding what is disapproved (al-munkar) amounts to turning away from the commands, even if the one who is slack is diligent in action, He said, emphasizing it as an alert to the gravity of the matter because of the multitude of enemies and the continual harm and aggression: ﴿Let them not turn you away﴾, that is, the unbelievers, through their excessive aversion and their saying: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given?﴾ [al-Qasas: 48] and the like of it,

﴿from the signs of God﴾, that is, from proclaiming them openly, and they are from the One characterized by the attributes of perfection, at the times that exist ﴿after they have been sent down﴾, that is, after their sending down occurred from the One who knows, reaching ﴿to you﴾, with what you see of its commands and prohibitions. This meaning has been clarified by His saying: ﴿And call﴾, that is, bring about the calling of people ﴿to your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you, for His goodness to you and His turning toward you alone, above the creation. He left out emphasis here, relying on what is within capacity, for the verb is not intended to be pursued with extreme intensity, indicating that securing benefits (jalb al-masalih) is easier in its difficulty than warding off corruptions (dar' al-mafasid), since what is required in the latter is the utmost limit, bounded by abstention. (p-381) Since one who keeps silent about the doer of the disapproved act is a partner to him, He said, emphasizing it as an alert to the concern with warding off corruptions, and that in this there must be reaching the goal: ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾, that is, counted among their ranks by leaving off forbidding them from their polytheism and what results from it for even a single hour.

When what comes from a people is described by what each of them is characterized by, and their participation in it is by action, which is further removed than their participation by silence, He said, without emphasis: ﴿And do not call upon another god along with Allah﴾, meaning the One who combines all the attributes of perfection, ﴿a god﴾. Since an indefinite noun in the context of a prohibition is general, just as it is in the context of a negation, and since the polytheists had shown obstinacy when they saw the Prophet ﷺ calling upon "Allah" and "al-Rahman," as mentioned at the end of surah al-Isra', He said: ﴿another﴾ [meaning] other than Allah in reality, not merely differing in name while being the same in essence. This was discussed at the end of surah al-Hijr, and what clarifies this meaning will come, if Allah the Most High wills, in surah al-Dhariyat. The purpose of all of this is to intensify the warning, informing that one who abandons forbidding evil while able to do so is a partner of the one who commits it, even if he does not himself perpetrate it. The Prophet ﷺ was able to do so by the protection of Allah the Most High for him. Then He gave the reason for this in His words: ﴿There is no god but Him﴾, meaning, so that He alone deserves to be the object of a servant's devotion. Then He gave the reason for His oneness in His words: ﴿Everything is perishing﴾, meaning (p-382) it is in the state of perishing and annihilation, and deserves this because it is contingent (mumkin), ﴿except His Face﴾, meaning He Himself. He is the Everlasting, because He is the Necessary Existent (wajib al-wujud), and the existence of every existing thing is only through Him. Perhaps He expressed the Essence by "Face" so as to include what is intended by it of righteous deeds, together with what is well known of its permissibility for this reason, being the most noble part, and because looking toward it is what moves one to obedience through shyness and what is similar to it. Then He gave the reason for this in His words: ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾, meaning, to Allah alone. The pronoun here is an istikhdam (a figure in which a word is used in one sense and its pronoun in another), ﴿the judgment﴾, meaning the decisive action grounded in all-pervasive knowledge over everything, and there is no judgment for anything over Him. ﴿And to Him alone you will be returned﴾ in all your conditions: in this world, in that no one's will takes effect except by His will, and in the Hereafter by resurrection, so that He rewards the doer of good for his goodness and the disobedient for his disobedience. There is no doubt that these commands and prohibitions, although their address is directed to Him ﷺ, are intended for his followers. Perhaps they were directed to him ﷺ because the command of a leader is more effective in bringing his followers to acceptance. It has become clear through this exposition, within these fine meanings, that this Book is clear, and through the execution of His will, glorified and exalted, in strengthening the weak among the Children of Israel, contrary to what Pharaoh and Qarun and their followers among the people of haughtiness intended, by the obedience of water and earth and what gathered the elements, namely the hand and the staff, that to Him alone belongs the judgment (p-383) over what He wills and chooses. Thus it is correct that the return is to Him on the Day of Return, the Day on which no soul speaks except by His permission. Thus the end of the surah corresponds to its beginning, and its summary is opened up by its detailed explanation.
